provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Mech family batch. Vertical crowded with fake listings and bait pricing, so every line leans on being a provably real, local locksmith. Low ticket, so prices are small. No lock, safe or key-machine brands, no arrival-time promises, licence shown only as a placeholder.

pageStructurePlus.section: Proof you're a real local locksmith
pageStructurePlus.contains: Shop or home-base address, the owner's name and face, the marked van, a bracketed state locksmith licence where the state requires one, and how to spot a fake locksmith listing
pageStructurePlus.why: Locksmith searches are full of call centres posing as local shops. Customers who have been burned choose the one that proves it is a real person nearby.

pageStructurePlus.section: Car key and fob replacement by vehicle
pageStructurePlus.contains: Transponder keys, remote fobs, push-to-start keys, all keys lost versus a spare, what to have ready like the VIN and registration, and cutting keys on site
pageStructurePlus.why: Car key buyers compare the locksmith with the dealer. Showing which vehicles you can do on site, without a tow, wins that comparison.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Moving into a new home, lost keys, an ex-tenant or ex-partner, one key for every door, rekeying versus new deadbolts, and what each involves
pageStructurePlus.why: New homeowners don't know rekeying exists. Explaining it turns a lockout customer into a whole-house rekey job.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What ID the locksmith asks for at a house or car lockout, proof of residence or registration, and why the check protects the customer
pageStructurePlus.why: Honest locksmiths ask for ID and scammers don't. Explaining the check up front turns an annoyance into a trust signal.

pageStructurePlus.section: Business locks and master key systems
pageStructurePlus.contains: Commercial deadbolts, panic bars, master key systems with restricted keys, key control logs, and lock changes after an employee leaves
pageStructurePlus.why: Small business owners need a locksmith they can call again and again. A commercial page turns one call into an account.

designDirections.name: Night Shift
designDirections.bestFor: Solo mobile locksmiths taking lockout and car key calls from a single van
designDirections.headlineSample: Locked out in {City}? A local locksmith, not a call centre
designDirections.whyItFits: Gunmetal with a mono-forward type reads like a working tool case at night, and puts the owner's name and address where a fake listing has none.

designDirections.name: Lockout Line
designDirections.bestFor: Locksmith shops with two or more vans covering lockouts, car keys, rekeys and small business accounts
designDirections.headlineSample: Lockouts, car keys and rekeys in {City}, from a real local shop
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo. Mono labels for the trip fee, hours and shop address make the pricing look honest, which is what beats bait-price listings.

designDirections.name: Old Key Shop
designDirections.bestFor: Storefront locksmiths with safes, high-security locks, period door hardware and commercial accounts
designDirections.headlineSample: {City}'s locksmith shop for safes, high-security locks and keys
designDirections.whyItFits: Brick, linen and a slab display feel like an old key shop with a bench and a counter, the opposite of an anonymous lead-gen page.

openers.line: {Business Name} looks like a real local locksmith on the map, with a real address and reviews, but there's no website. The fake locksmith listings around you all have one.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A locksmith site that proves you're the real one: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing points to a Facebook page. Someone locked out of their car wants to see your name, your van and your trip fee in ten seconds, not scroll posts.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the latest locksmith post.
openers.linkLine: A locksmith page built for a lockout on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your locksmith site uses the same template and stock van as the lead-gen listings. Honestly, it makes a real shop look like one of the fakes.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for stock vans, no address, or a generic template. Note what you found.

openers.angle: Hard to tap on a phone
openers.line: On my phone your locksmith page hides the number below a big banner. Someone standing outside a locked door at night has about thirty seconds of patience.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note whether the number taps. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your locksmith site with the number up top: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to send {Business Name} the make, model and year for a car key quote. People who lost their only key would rather type it than be put on hold.
openers.hook: Check the listing, the social pages and any site for a key request form. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A car key request that asks for the vehicle: {demo-link}

openers.line: Every new homeowner in {City} should rekey, and almost none know it's cheaper than new locks. A rekey page from a local locksmith catches them the week they get the keys.
openers.hook: Look for any rekey posts or reviews from new homeowners. Quote one if you find it.
openers.linkLine: A rekey page for new homeowners: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews keep saying you charged what you quoted on the phone. In the locksmith trade that line is gold, and it's sitting where nobody comparing locksmiths will read it.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy a phrase about honest pricing or a fast lockout. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those honest-price locksmith reviews up front: {demo-link}

openers.line: Summer is moving season in {City}, which means new keys, lost keys and landlords changing locks between tenants. The locksmith with a clear rekey page gets those calls.
openers.hook: Use this in late spring or before the end-of-month move-in rush. Name the season in the reply.

openers.line: Most lockouts happen late, after a night out or a shift. If your locksmith line rolls to a full voicemail, that person calls the next listing, which is often a call centre.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If it goes to a full or generic voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A lockout request that works late at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for an apprentice locksmith. People who want to learn the trade check whether a shop is real and established, same as customers.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or story. Note the date of the post.
openers.linkLine: A locksmith shop page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing online says your locksmith van covers {Neighborhood}. Fake listings claim every neighbourhood, so a real list of where you actually go stands out.
openers.hook: Find neighbourhoods named in their reviews. Use the furthest one.
openers.linkLine: A locksmith service map that's actually true: {demo-link}

openers.line: A few of your reviews are from shops and offices. Small businesses rekey every time someone quits, and they want one locksmith they can call every time.
openers.hook: Only if reviews mention a business, office or store. Quote one.
openers.linkLine: A business locks and master key page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your state keeps a locksmith register, but customers never check it. Showing your licence and your name on a page is the one thing the fake locksmith listings can't copy.
openers.hook: Check whether their state licenses locksmiths and whether they appear. Note it exists; never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, name and shop address on one locksmith page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like most of your locksmith work comes from regulars and local shops. Every new resident in {City} searches instead, and finds the fakes first.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'our locksmith for years'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a new resident would find a real locksmith: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is careful locksmith work, a clean deadbolt fit with no chewed wood. Work like that proves you're real better than any ad.
openers.hook: Pick their newest posted job and name it exactly: rekey, car key, safe or business lock.
openers.linkLine: That locksmith job, front and centre: {demo-link}

objections.objection: The fake listings outrank everyone. A site won't help.
objections.handler: "It won't beat every fake on day one. It gives the people who do find you, through reviews or a referral, proof you're real, so they don't hang up and try the next number."

objections.objection: Lockouts are cheap jobs. I can't spend much.
objections.handler: "That's why it's priced for a locksmith, not a remodeler. The rekey, car key and business pages are where the bigger tickets are, and a few of those cover it."

objections.objection: I don't want to post prices. The scammers undercut them.
objections.handler: "We post your trip fee and how you quote, not a bait number. Customers burned by a fake locksmith trust the one who's upfront."
"The site takes car key requests with the vehicle details while you're on a lockout. I need about an hour of your time in total."

objections.objection: A friend built my site for free.
objections.handler: "If it shows your name, address and van, keep it. If it looks like the template sites, happy to hand over the 'real locksmith' and rekey pages."
"{Build Range}. For you, about {Build Price}. A handful of rekeys or car keys booked through it covers that."

The locksmith site is still ready, same price. {demo-link} for another look.

bullets: Low-ticket trade: keep the build at the bottom of the board range and sell proof of being local, not a showcase.
The 'real local locksmith' page is the core. Without the owner's name and address on it, nothing else works.
Price car key and rekey pages separately; they carry the bigger tickets in this trade.
Never post a trip fee, licence number or arrival window the owner hasn't given you; use bracketed fields.
Commercial master key pages only for locksmiths who already serve businesses.
Recurring add-ons stay small. A locksmith judges everything against a lockout fee.

lineItems.description: Max with the owner's story, shop or base address map, van shot placeholders and a fake-listing warning checklist.

Max with a new-homeowner checklist, door count picker and a rekey request form.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests naming the locksmith
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After every lockout or rekey, the customer gets a text asking for a review that mentions the locksmith's name. Named reviews are what fake listings can't fake."

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile verification and cleanup
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "I tidy your Google profile so the address, hours and van shots match the site exactly, and report the fake locksmith listings sitting on your street."

whatElseYouSell.name: Weekly locksmith job posts on the profile
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A real rekey, car key or safe job posted to your Google profile each week, so the listing looks alive and local."

whatElseYouSell.name: Realtor and landlord rekey card
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A leave-behind card for realtors and landlords offering rekeys at closing or between tenants, with the locksmith booking page on it."

whatElseYouSell.name: Van lettering with name and address
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Lettering with your shop name, address and site on the locksmith van. Customers who've read about scams look for exactly that when it pulls up."

whatElseYouSell.name: Key tag and keychain giveaways
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every key you cut goes out on a tag with your locksmith number, so the next lockout calls you from memory, not a search."

whatElseYouSell.name: Small business lock check mailer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A postcard to shops and offices nearby offering a lock and key-control check, from the locksmith already working on that block."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the business page is live.

withoutAI.route: Realtors who order rekeys at closing
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The agents who call you to rekey after closing need a vendor page for their buyers. Your locksmith shop is the first name on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Realtors live on a trusted vendor list and rarely present it well.

withoutAI.whoPays: The door installer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Whoever hangs new entry doors in {City} needs a locksmith for the hardware, and a site of their own. Your rekey page links to them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Door installers and locksmiths share every new entry door job.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The alarm and camera installer you refer to sells to the same worried homeowners. Their site is usually a catalogue with no local face."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Security installers and locksmiths swap referrals after every break-in.

withoutAI.route: Small landlords changing locks between tenants
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Landlords who rekey every turnover need a simple maintenance request page. Lock changes route to your locksmith van."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Turnover rekeys are steady work, and landlords want one trusted locksmith.

withoutAI.route: Auto repair shops and used car lots
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The car lots that call you for spare keys before a sale have weak inventory sites. Your car key work gets me the introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Used car lots need second keys constantly and trust the locksmith who makes them.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Storage facilities call you to cut locks on unpaid units. Their sites rarely let anyone reserve a unit, and your locksmith work opens the door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Independent storage owners need booking sites and already rely on a locksmith.

withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant builds each buyer's after-closing checklist, utilities, rekeying the locks, address change, and books the locksmith from it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents want to look helpful after closing, and the locksmith client gets every rekey.

withAI.pitchLine: "When a tenant gives notice, an assistant lines up cleaning, repairs and the lock change with the locksmith, and texts each vendor."
withAI.whyItWorks: Turnovers are chaotic, and the locksmith rides along on every one.

withAI.route: Incident report drafts for security installers
withAI.pitchLine: "After a break-in, an assistant drafts the customer's summary of camera clips and recommended upgrades, including the locksmith's door hardware."
withAI.whyItWorks: Security firms want to look thorough after an incident, and lock upgrades flow to the locksmith.

withAI.route: Lien-sale notice drafts for storage owners
withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant drafts overdue-unit notices from the owner's own templates and schedules the locksmith for the lock cut, for the owner to review."
withAI.whyItWorks: Storage owners juggle notices by hand, and every cut lock is locksmith work.

withAI.route: Vehicle listing writer for car lots
withAI.pitchLine: "Photograph the car and the window sticker, and an assistant drafts the listing, including whether a spare key comes with it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Small lots list cars slowly, and the locksmith's introduction gets the meeting.

withAI.route: Quote follow-up for the door installer
withAI.pitchLine: "The door installer you work with loses quotes to slow replies. Automatic follow-up, set up the same way as your locksmith texts."
withAI.whyItWorks: It's configuration of something you've built, with a trusted introduction.

softwareAI.name: Lockout call catcher
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A missed call gets a text asking whether it's a house or car lockout and where they are, so the locksmith calls back the stranded one first."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the business number forwarded and the wording approved.

softwareAI.name: Car key quote lookup by vehicle
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter make, model and year and the locksmith's own price range for a key or fob shows up, so the quote on the phone is instant and consistent."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price list by key type and the vehicles they can do.

softwareAI.name: Named review replies for the locksmith
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every review gets a reply drafted in the owner's voice that names the lockout, rekey or car key job, which shows searchers a real locksmith answers."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with review requests running. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: ID and ownership capture at the door
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The locksmith snaps the customer's ID and proof of residence or registration, and it's stored with the job record, which protects you if a lockout is ever questioned."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their current ID policy and how long they keep records.

softwareAI.name: Key code and master key records
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every business master key system, its pinning chart and who holds which key, kept securely so a lost key means a quick rekey, not a re-plan."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, for locksmiths with business accounts. Needs their existing charts.

softwareAI.name: After-hours lockout answering line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers late lockout calls, explains the trip fee and the ID check, takes the location and wakes the locksmith only when the caller agrees."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their fee wording and on-call rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Rekey booking with door count
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New homeowners book a rekey online, choose how many doors, and see the locksmith's price before the visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their rekey pricing and availability.

softwareAI.name: Q&A assistant on locks and keys
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can you make a key for my car without the original' and 'is rekeying cheaper than new locks' from the locksmith's notes, and books a visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their FAQ notes and vehicle list. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Business account billing for locksmith work
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Shops and landlords get one monthly statement for every rekey and lock change, sent automatically with a card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their account list and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Scam-call pattern notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It reads the locksmith's call notes and flags callers who say a 'locksmith' quoted low then tripled the price, so you can post honest warnings for {City}."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a few months of call notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; it never names a business.

softwareAI.name: Fob and key blank stock tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Track key blanks and fobs in the van by vehicle, and get a reorder list before a car key call has to be turned away."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their current stock list.

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to locksmith invoice
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Say the job, lockout, rekey of four cylinders or a programmed fob, and the locksmith invoice is drafted with the ID record attached."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their invoice template. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Moving-season rekey reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Realtor partners and landlords get a reminder text before the end-of-month move-ins, with locksmith rekey slots to book."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the partner list.

softwareAI.name: Locksmith van schedule
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Lockouts, rekeys and business jobs on one board by van, so the nearest locksmith takes the urgent call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, at two vans. Needs job types and how they dispatch today.

softwareAI.name: Address history for lock work
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Type the address and see every lock, rekey and key cut done there, and who was verified as the owner each time."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past job notes.

softwareAI.name: Profit by locksmith job type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether lockouts, car keys or rekeys make the shop money once blanks, fobs, fuel and drive time are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs a season of invoices.

softwareAI.name: Employee-leaves lock change alerts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Business clients get a quarterly nudge to tell the locksmith about staff who've left, so restricted keys get recovered or locks rekeyed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, after the business account page. Needs the account list.

softwareAI.name: Vehicle key programming notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The locksmith's own notes on programming fobs by vehicle, searchable on the phone in the car, with what worked last time."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs a season of car key notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Apprentice locksmith training library
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The owner records how to pick, rekey and pin a cylinder, and it becomes a locksmith how-to library for the apprentice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, when they hire. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Locksmith applicant background pre-screen
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants confirm they'll pass the background check your state requires for locksmiths, can work nights and have a clean licence, before you call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: When they post a hiring note. Needs must-haves and state rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the real-locksmith site for honest shops
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every honest locksmith loses calls to fake listings. A site built around proof of being local is a product every one of them needs."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The problem is identical in every city, and low-ticket trades prefer a subscription.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The state or national locksmith association
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give the public a directory of verified member locksmiths with real addresses, so they can avoid the fakes."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations fight scam listings and want a public tool to do it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your counter sees every real locksmith in the region every week. A public locator of those shops is the best weapon against fake locksmith listings, and it keeps them buying blanks from you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want shop loyalty and see every real locksmith in the region.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The state or city consumer affairs office
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Locksmith scams are a standing complaint. A plain public guide on checking a locksmith, with licence lookups, answers it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Consumer offices have outreach budgets and recurring locksmith complaints.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "License my locksmith template, built to look real and local, instead of the generic one that makes clients look like fakes."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies need a build that doesn't resemble lead-gen pages.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your turnover lock changes across many doors need one portal with locksmith booking and key records."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Bigger managers want vendor visibility and will pay for it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your car lockout vendors have no way to show drivers who's coming. A vendor page kit for locksmiths in the network fixes that."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Roadside networks are judged on the vendor who shows up.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Storage owners need vetted locksmiths for lock cuts in every town. A member directory of locksmiths who do them solves it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations want useful member resources, and lock cuts are a constant need.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Car dealer service department key referrals
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "When a customer needs a key the same day and service is booked out, a page referring them to a vetted local locksmith keeps them happy."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Dealers lose goodwill on key delays, and the locksmith becomes the referral.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A new-home checklist page for every customer the movers serve, with a vetted locksmith for the rekey on move-in day."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Movers want to add value at delivery, and rekeys are the natural first job.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A locksmith shop in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one real locksmith per metro. {City} has one; the next metro's most trusted locksmith is still being buried by fakes."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The template and the anti-scam pitch carry straight over.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Safe technicians who open, move and service safes serve banks, jewellers and gun owners, and need a sharper site than a lockout locksmith."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Higher-ticket specialists pay more, and the premium direction is already designed.

upsellLadder.offer: Car key quote lookup by vehicle
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of car key requests with vehicle details.
upsellLadder.line: "You've quoted the same car keys over and over. Let's make the locksmith quote instant."

upsellLadder.trigger: A realtor or landlord books a rekey.
upsellLadder.line: "A landlord booked a rekey. Let's put a locksmith card in every agent's and landlord's hand before moving season."
